the internal scattering of open cylindrical structures with various terminations is a complex phenomenon that is affected by a variety of factors.
the monostatic RCS of the open cylinder with the short-circuit flat-plate termination is the same as that of a solid cylinder.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the following three problems: (1) the RCS of a short-circuited open cylinder, (2) the RCS of an open cylinder terminated by a coaxial plug, and (3) the RCS and the modulated energy of an open cylinder terminating in a set of copplanar blades.
the internal scattering from an open cylinder, which has three different terminations: a short-circuited plate, a plug, and a set blades.
the scattering of an open conducting cylinder with complex terminators.

the RCS of the open cylinder with the blades is much lower than that of the shorted cylinder.
, as the number of blades is increased, the monostatic RCS decreases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the monostatic RCS of the cylinder with a short-circular plate or plug termination is independent of the frequency of the incident wave, while the monostatic scattering from the cylinder with blades is dependent on the frequency and the rotation of the blades.
the monostatic RCS of the cylinder is strongly dependent on the termination, and the spectral energy of scattered wave is dependent not only on the termination, but also on the blade rotation.
we have developed a rigorous solution for the scattering of an open cylindrical structure with arbitrary terminations, and we have applied this solution to the three cases of interest.

for all the cases considered, the monostatic RCS is significantly enhanced when the terminations are present.
